## Warsh發言前美債小跌，聯準會內部對緊縮程度看法分歧

Warsh首度在傑克森洞會議發言前，美債小幅走弱。初領失業救濟人數維持低檔，部分官員又呼籲收緊政策，使$440億7年期公債標售的穩健需求未能帶動債市轉強。2年、10年及30年期殖利率各升1個基點，收在4.20%、4.67%及5.19%。10年期損益兩平通膨率升至2.33%，實質殖利率維持2.34%；曲線不變，2s10s為47個基點，2s30s為99。

堪薩斯市聯準銀行總裁Schmid認為，短期利率可能仍偏寬鬆；克里夫蘭的Hammack則主張現在就應行動，因為現行政策不足以讓經濟降溫。其他官員仍認為可以等待。分歧不只在於何時再升息，而是目前利率究竟有沒有達到限制性水準。市場仍僅給予9月升息約三分之一的機率，但已反映年底前升息25個基點。

Nvidia財測帶動股市大漲，漲勢卻高度集中。Nasdaq 100上漲1.43%，半導體指數漲2.33%；S&P 500雖有多數成分股下跌，指數仍漲0.72%。VIX下滑4.60%至14.51。Nvidia亮眼成長前景之外，也披露龐大的採購承諾與保證，使債券投資人持續關注傳統借款以外的負擔。

荷姆茲外交協商遇到阻礙，油價回升。WTI上漲1.57%至$83.52，布蘭特漲0.82%至$88.56；不過，海峽實際運量已恢復到每日約600萬至800萬桶，約為戰前的一半。整體信用債ETF變化不大。美債跌幅有限、標售順利、曲線未變，較像是Warsh發言前的審慎調整，而非市場全面重新評價美國長天期風險。海外則已有實際行動：韓國、菲律賓與盧安達升息，澳洲市場也提前反映下一次緊縮。

## Schmid與Hammack要求收緊政策，失業救濟申請仍低

Schmid的立場接近7月支持升息的官員。聯邦資金目標區間為3.5%至3.75%，PCE年增率卻達3.7%，因此他質疑短端政策是否具有抑制作用。Hammack是7月主張升息25個基點的三名異議官員之一，她認為利率尚未充分壓低經濟熱度，現在就應採取行動。

Hammack預估2026年底通膨仍接近3%，明年也只會緩慢降向2.5%左右。她表示通膨預期尚未失去錨定，但連續五年多高於目標，終究可能改變家庭行為。股權與債券資本市場異常活躍，也加深她對金融條件是否足夠緊縮的疑慮。

波士頓聯準銀行總裁Collins仍從房市與小企業看到溫和抑制效果。她今年沒有投票權，支持7月維持利率；能否繼續等待，取決於通膨是否下降，尤其在關稅、中東情勢或其他供應衝擊持續時。她也認為通膨預期仍與2%目標一致。芝加哥的Goolsbee則聚焦服務價格：若降溫，可以繼續等待；若維持高檔甚至惡化，就會更加擔心。這些差異顯示，Schmid與Hammack的主張尚未成為委員會共識。

截至8月22日當週，初領失業救濟人數由修正後20.7萬降至20.3萬，低於預估的20.8萬；續領人數為177.8萬。7月商品貿易赤字初值則從$1,014億擴大至$1,188億，明顯高於預估的$990億。赤字增加$174億，使成長率估算更複雜，但僅憑總額，無法判定國內需求或庫存各占多少影響。相較之下，失業救濟資料更直接顯示，就業市場沒有突然轉弱。

一筆大宗交易買進4.5萬口10月聯邦資金期貨，其方向符合12月前不升息的判斷；整體市場定價則仍保留約三分之一的9月升息機率。這種部位與鷹派官員說法之間的落差，也說明短端為何沒有帶頭大幅下跌。

Warsh將在8月28日紐約時間上午10點發言，年度就業人數基準修正初值也同時公布。前次基準修正為下調91.1萬人。如果這次再大幅下修，可能改變對就業成長的評估，但不代表最新每週失業救濟人數失效。投資人將同時收到可能相當重要的就業基準調整，以及主席對政策框架的說明。

## Nvidia成長財測伴隨龐大承諾，企業拓展籌資管道

Nvidia預估2028會計年度營收約成長70%，高於分析師原估的45%；當期營收預估為$1,080億，年增89%。股價上漲近9%，市值增加約$4,420億。較小型客戶貢獻約$400億、占當季營收42%，比重超過一年前的兩倍，需求不再只集中於最大幾家雲端業者。不過，記憶體、晶圓及封裝仍是供應瓶頸。

為滿足需求而興建的設施，正與其他產業爭取勞工、設備、材料及電力。即使住宅建築疲弱，商品生產與建築業薪資增速仍相對服務業加快；Schmid也特別提及轄區內AI投資造成的競爭。聯準會要判斷的是，這些壓力會向相關專案以外擴散多少。當日損益兩平通膨率只升1個基點，不足以據此認定單一原因。

Nvidia披露未來支出承諾達$2,790億，其中相當部分涉及三星電子、SK海力士、美光及台積電。此外，公司承諾支付至多$560億資料中心使用費，即使未使用容量也可能須付款；另承擔$1,090億貸款保證，多數與OpenAI在俄亥俄州的大型資料中心有關。這些法律義務各不相同，不能當成同一種債務相加看待，但足以說明：若交付、使用率或交易對手表現不如預期，公司可能需要投入多少現金或信用支持。

大型雲端業者今年已透過七種幣別募集超過$2,200億。摩根大通歐洲投資級融資主管Matthias Reschke估計，這些公司在美國的利差，比其他企業債高約55個基點。他認為市場仍可承接，只是必須付出相應價格。轉向較小幣別能擴大買方來源，也可能讓這些公司迅速成為當地最主要的非金融借款人。

摩根大通已開始接洽貸款機構，為Volta Infrastructure資料中心安排$50億融資。這家新公司先前以$24億估值取得$3億創投資金，並與Anthropic簽下六年、$100億合約，由其與Bitdeer Technologies共同管理的挪威據點提供算力。客戶合約提供營收基礎，但槓桿、擔保品、攤還、保證及建設執行等條件，仍須由貸款人確認。

Fortescue考慮首次發行熊貓債，擬透過Fortescue Treasury (China)募集約CN¥30億，由母公司提供保證；投資人會議預計在9月初，可能於10月行銷。公司已申請兩年內發行至多CN¥200億。今年熊貓債平均票息1.88%，比3年期美債殖利率低逾200個基點，可提供另一籌資管道。與此同時，公司與中國國有鐵礦石買方的爭議正干擾部分出口。上述票息差並非納入匯率避險後的成本比較。

Moderna則利用癌症疫苗試驗利多帶來的股價窗口。8月19日股價單日上漲177%後，公司宣布發行$20億、2032年到期的優先可轉債，另有$3億增額選擇權，用於疫苗業務及還債。較高股價有利提高轉換價格，減少日後轉換所需股數；但公告後盤前股價仍跌5%，投資人同時評估稀釋與新增供給。

## 韓國實際升息，澳洲重新定價，日本準備加快腳步

韓國央行以6比1決議，將7天期附買回利率提高25個基點至3%，連續第二次升息，也是三年多來首次接連緊縮。總裁申鉉松表示，預先採取行動是為避免日後付出更高代價。半導體強勢促使央行將2026年成長預估從2.6%提高至3.3%，2027年預估2.9%；通膨預估維持今年2.7%、明年2.3%。六個月利率指引的21個點中，有10個落在3.25%，顯示再升一次仍有相當可能。韓元一度升至每美元1,377.30。

菲律賓則在成長明顯較弱時升息。央行連續第三次上調25個基點，逆附買回目標利率升至5%，符合25名經濟學家中20人的預期。通膨約為目標的兩倍，央行預估2026及2027年平均通膨均高於4%的容許上限，到2028年才回到3%左右。進口石油、聖嬰現象及工資仍帶來風險；第2季GDP成長2.3%，低於預期，在東南亞主要經濟體中僅優於泰國。

盧安達央行升息50個基點至8.75%，為2009年以來最高，也是連續第三次調升。都市通膨自4月起維持雙位數，受生鮮食品、肉類及能源推動，已達14.5%。央行預估2026年通膨13.1%、2027年7.9%，反映聖嬰與中東風險仍在，政策目標區間則為2%至8%。

澳洲的調整主要出現在預測與債市。通膨偏熱後，澳洲聯邦銀行、澳盛及高盛轉向預期11月升息，德意志銀行與澳洲國民銀行則預期9月。市場已完全反映11月前升息25個基點，9月機率約五成。3年期公債殖利率上升7個基點至4.67%，創一個多月高點。7月家庭支出月增1.1%、年增7%；但仍有經濟學家預期不動，理由包括成長疲弱、房價下跌，以及澳洲央行對單月通膨數據的審慎態度。

日本央行副總裁冰見野良三要求更加注意物價上行風險，也未反駁9月升息預期。交換市場反映約82%的機率，談話前後變化有限；由於沒有比市場原先預期更明確的承諾，日圓一度貶至每美元159.40。若9月升息，將創植田和男任內最短的升息間隔。冰見野表示，等待所有資訊齊備，可能迫使央行日後更劇烈地調整。不過，單次升息對承受利差及油品進口壓力的日圓，幫助可能有限：聯合干預曾將匯價從約164推升至155.23，如今又回到接近160。

歐洲央行7月會議紀錄顯示，部分成員原可支持升息，甚至質疑是否還有避免再次調升的可能，但最終全體同意按兵不動。存款利率目前2.25%，首席經濟學家Lane認為中性區間上緣是2.5%；官員討論是否需要溫和限制性的政策，才能讓通膨回到2%。紀錄顯示緊縮主張獲得更多支持，但對過度抑制經濟的擔憂並未消失。

泰國央行總裁Vitai Ratanakorn反駁利率將長期維持1%的市場假設，但也表示目前證據不足以支持調整。持續通膨或泰銖急貶可能需要升息，新經濟衝擊則可能需要降息；再寬鬆未必能透過銀行有效傳導，還會減少存款人收入及政策空間。相較前一天的維持利率決策，這次新增的重點是：未來方向仍可能向上，也可能向下。

## 瑞銀AT1替代方案受檢視，萬科虧損持續擴大

瑞士國會議員正考慮重新設計AT1，讓瑞銀以較低成本滿足約$200億新增資本要求的一部分。政府主張，海外子公司應完全由普通股權益第一類資本支應。瑞銀約占€2,860億歐洲AT1市場的7%，因此制度設計不只影響單一發行人。

影響國會討論的學術方案建議，銀行跌破法定資本要求時，AT1息票、普通股股利及管理層獎金應一併停止支付；若仍無法恢復資本，可在辦理現金增資時，提供AT1持有人自願轉股選項。用意是在銀行仍持續營運時吸收損失，而非等到救援或處置才發揮作用。瑞信$170億AT1減記造成的訴訟與投資人疑慮，至今未解。

財政部長Karin Keller-Sutter認為，普通股才是持續營運狀態下唯一可靠的損失吸收工具，瑞士央行也支持海外業務全額以CET1支應。替代方案還須取得國際監管機關與投資人接受。上院經濟委員會預計8月31日討論，最終由國會決定；目前仍是提案，並非已同意修改既有AT1條款。

中國萬科上半年虧損由一年前CN¥119.5億擴大至CN¥149.5億，2024年以來累計虧損達CN¥1,530億。即使已展延10檔公開債券，營運資金仍吃緊。深圳地鐵去年提供超過CN¥300億貸款，今年上半年再提供CN¥45億，協助支付展延所需的前期款項，卻尚未恢復營運現金創造能力。萬科3.975%美元債約在55美分交易，3.5%券約51美分。

一檔原訂去年底到期的3%人民幣債，展延後將於12月中到期。萬科表示，會為明年6月以前到期的公開債券制定償付計畫，包括可能再次展延。深圳當局已安排由國有背景高管主導的董事會，但股東後續支持的規模及順位仍不明確。

美國高收益市政債則出現投資人在困境發生前就拒絕交易的情況。今年發行額$33億，比去年的紀錄步調慢約5%，同期整體市政債發行卻快約6%。休士頓非營利組織QCF/I在銀行將擬議殖利率提高至8%後，仍撤下未評級發債，另有一項未評級專案也未能售出。較高品質債券已有不錯的絕對收益，而承擔低品質風險的額外補償偏窄，降低買方追逐收益的誘因。目前33起首次違約、合計$28.1億，仍接近歷史經驗，失敗交易尚不代表全市場關閉。

## 哥倫比亞付息負擔上升，印尼與印度各有匯率壓力

哥倫比亞新政府計畫在2028年恢復前任政府暫停的財政規則，並提出法案，將初級赤字降低相當於GDP的2.2個百分點。但眼前預算相當吃緊：2027年整體赤字預估占GDP 9.4%，支出增加16%至COP635兆，約$2,010億。

其中債務本息支出將增加逾50%至COP155兆，經常支出COP393兆，投資COP87兆；計畫借款約COP239兆，63%來自國內、37%來自海外。政府表示，正在認列前任低估的負債。透明度提高、未來恢復財政規則，有助重建公信力，但調整生效前，投資人仍須承接眼前因付息負擔上升而增加的融資。

印尼數千人在國會外抗議貪腐、生活成本及政府問責問題。議員承諾12月15日前通過資產沒收法，否則辭職，使午後升高的緊張情勢逐漸緩和。印尼盾盤中最多貶0.4%，收盤貶0.1%至每美元17,726；10年期殖利率上升3個基點至7.08%，債市連續第三天下跌。隨大規模暴力衝突疑慮降低，股市收漲1.8%。

這次抗議聯盟比一年前的全國性運動規模小、整合程度低，主要學生及勞工團體未參與，也有助市場盤中回穩。一些投資人事前已從印尼盾債轉向美元債，反映的是降低匯率曝險，不一定是全面退出印尼主權債。

印度央行則更經常在盧比轉弱時進場，6月以來$730億美元流入提供支撐，上月某一天即動用$70億。干預使短期盧比波動接近十個月低點，但油價上升仍擴大經常帳赤字，與美國的利差也在縮小。交易更平穩，並未減少進口支出或護匯消耗的儲備。

## 就業修正與Warsh同時登場，後續再看融資條件

8月28日就業基準修正與Warsh談話同時公布，解讀時須區分歷史就業水準調整與主席對通膨的判斷。大幅下修可能支持繼續等待，但若Warsh認同Schmid與Hammack所說的政策抑制不足，訊號便可能相反。2至5年期對預期升息日期改變最敏感。

澳洲第2季GDP及勞動數據，將檢驗消費與通膨強勢是否足以壓過房市疲弱。日本方面，植田預計在G20聚會後發言，隨後還有高田創及Kazuyuki Masu的談話，可進一步觀察央行對縮短升息間隔的態度。兩地市場已反映相當程度緊縮，因此重點是官員與資料能確認多少既有預期。

信用市場接下來看Volta的$50億方案，如何把Anthropic合約落實為擔保品、攤還及股東支持條款。瑞士8月31日委員會討論，則將顯示AT1替代方案能否向前推進，或普通股資本主張仍占上風。長期客戶合約與資本工具構想本身，都要等實際條款確定後，才能判斷損失由誰承擔。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Treasuries edge lower before Warsh as Fed officials question the degree of restraint

Treasuries edged lower ahead of Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole address, with firm jobless claims and calls for tighter policy offsetting solid demand at a $44 billion 7-year auction. Two-, 10- and 30-year yields each rose 1 basis point, to 4.20%, 4.67% and 5.19%. Ten-year breakevens increased to 2.33% while real yields stayed at 2.34%; the curve was unchanged, with 2s10s at 47 basis points and 2s30s at 99.

Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said short-term rates might still be accommodative. Cleveland's Beth Hammack wanted officials to act now, arguing that policy was not slowing the economy enough. Other officials saw room to wait. The disagreement was more fundamental than the timing of another increase: policymakers differed over whether the current setting was restrictive in the first place. Markets continued to assign only about a one-third chance to September tightening, while pricing 25 basis points by year-end.

Nvidia's outlook drove a strong but concentrated equity rally. The Nasdaq 100 gained 1.43%, semiconductors rose 2.33%, and the S&P 500 added 0.72% despite declines in most constituents. VIX fell 4.60% to 14.51. The company's growth forecast also came with substantial purchase commitments and guarantees, keeping credit investors focused on obligations beyond conventional borrowing.

Oil recovered as Hormuz diplomacy encountered obstacles. WTI rose 1.57% to $83.52 and Brent 0.82% to $88.56, although physical flows through the strait had recovered to roughly 6 million–8 million barrels a day, about half the prewar level. Broad credit funds barely changed. The small Treasury loss, successful auction and unchanged curve showed caution before Warsh rather than a wholesale reassessment of US duration. Abroad, Korea, the Philippines and Rwanda actually raised rates, while Australian markets brought another hike closer.

## Schmid and Hammack press for tighter policy; claims remain low

Schmid placed himself close to the officials who had favored a July increase. With the federal funds target at 3.5%–3.75% and annual PCE inflation at 3.7%, he questioned whether short-end policy was restrictive at all. Hammack, one of July's three dissenters in favor of a quarter-point hike, said rates were not cooling the economy sufficiently and officials should act now.

Hammack expected inflation to end 2026 near 3% and make only limited progress toward the mid-2% range next year. Expectations had not become unanchored, she said, but more than five years above target could eventually change household behavior. Exceptionally active equity and debt capital markets added to her doubts about the degree of financial restraint.

Boston Fed President Susan Collins continued to see mild restriction in housing and small businesses. She is a nonvoter this year and supported July's hold; further patience depends on inflation easing, particularly if tariffs, Middle East developments or other supply shocks persist. She still judged expectations consistent with the 2% objective. Chicago's Austan Goolsbee focused on services prices: cooling would justify waiting, whereas sustained or worsening inflation would increase his concern. Those views left Schmid and Hammack short of an established committee consensus.

Initial jobless claims fell to 203,000 in the week ended August 22, from a revised 207,000 and below the 208,000 forecast. Continuing claims were 1.778 million. The advance July goods-trade deficit widened to $118.8 billion from $101.4 billion, against a forecast of $99 billion. That $17.4 billion deterioration complicates the growth estimate, but the headline alone does not identify how much came from domestic demand or inventories. Claims offered a clearer indication that the labor market had not weakened abruptly.

A block buyer acquired 45,000 October federal funds futures contracts in a trade consistent with no increase before December. Broader pricing still allowed roughly a one-third September probability. The disagreement between that positioning and the more forceful speakers helped explain why the front end did not lead a larger selloff.

Warsh speaks at 10 a.m. New York time on August 28, alongside the preliminary annual payroll revision. The prior benchmark revision was −911,000. A substantial new downward adjustment could change the assessment of employment growth without invalidating the latest weekly claims figure. Investors will hear the chair's policy framework at the same moment they receive a potentially important revision to the labor-market baseline.

## Nvidia's revenue outlook comes with large commitments; borrowers diversify funding

Nvidia forecast roughly 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, compared with the 45% analysts had expected, and current-period revenue of $108 billion, up 89% from a year earlier. Shares gained nearly 9%, adding about $442 billion in market value. Smaller customers generated around $40 billion, or 42%, of quarterly revenue—more than twice their share a year earlier—broadening demand beyond the largest hyperscalers. Memory, wafers and packaging remained supply constraints.

The construction needed to meet that demand is competing for workers, equipment, materials and electricity. Goods-producing and construction wage growth has accelerated relative to services despite weak housing construction. Schmid specifically cited competition from AI investment in his district. The issue for the Fed is how far those pressures spread beyond the projects themselves; the 1-basis-point breakeven increase was too small to establish a single cause.

Nvidia disclosed $279 billion of future spending commitments, much of it with Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, Micron and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. It also promised up to $56 billion for data-center use even if capacity goes unused and assumed $109 billion of loan guarantees, mostly tied to a large Ohio facility for OpenAI. These are different legal obligations, not interchangeable measures of debt. Together, however, they show how much cash or credit support could be required if delivery, utilization or counterparties disappoint.

Hyperscalers have raised more than $220 billion this year in seven currencies. JPMorgan's European investment-grade finance head Matthias Reschke estimated their US spread premium over other corporate debt at about 55 basis points. Issuance remained possible, he said, but at a price. Diversification into smaller currencies broadens the buyer base while potentially making these companies dominant nonfinancial borrowers in those markets.

JPMorgan has begun approaching lenders for a $5 billion package for Volta Infrastructure's data centers. The new company raised $300 million in venture funding at a $2.4 billion valuation and signed a six-year, $10 billion agreement to supply Anthropic with computing capacity at a Norwegian site managed with Bitdeer Technologies. The customer contract provides a revenue basis, but lenders still need final terms on leverage, collateral, amortization, guarantees and project execution.

Fortescue is considering its first panda bond: roughly 3 billion yuan through Fortescue Treasury (China), with a parent guarantee. Investor meetings are planned for early September and possible marketing for October. The company has applied to issue up to 20 billion yuan over two years. Panda bonds have carried an average 1.88% coupon this year, over 200 basis points below 3-year Treasury yields, offering funding diversification as a dispute with China's state-backed iron-ore buyer disrupts some exports. The coupon comparison alone is not a currency-hedged funding-cost calculation.

Moderna turned to convertible debt after positive cancer-vaccine trial results sent its shares up 177% on August 19. It announced $2 billion of senior convertibles due 2032, with an option for another $300 million, to fund the vaccine business and repay debt. A higher stock price can support a higher conversion price and reduce the eventual share count needed on conversion. The shares nevertheless fell 5% before the open after the announcement as investors assessed dilution and new supply.

## Korea leads actual hikes as Australia reprices and Japan signals readiness

The Bank of Korea raised its 7-day repo rate 25 basis points to 3% in a 6–1 vote, its second consecutive increase and first back-to-back tightening in more than three years. Governor Shin Hyun Song described the move as preemptive action to avoid a more costly response later. Semiconductor strength prompted the bank to lift its 2026 growth forecast to 3.3% from 2.6%; it forecast 2.9% for 2027. Inflation forecasts stayed at 2.7% this year and 2.3% next year. Ten of 21 points in six-month guidance were at 3.25%, suggesting another hike remained likely. The won strengthened as far as 1,377.30 per dollar.

The Philippines raised rates despite much weaker growth. A third consecutive 25-basis-point increase took the reverse-repo target to 5%, as 20 of 25 economists expected. Inflation was running at about twice target, and the central bank expected annual averages above the 4% tolerance ceiling in both 2026 and 2027 before returning near 3% in 2028. Oil imports, El Nino and wages remained risks. Q2 growth of 2.3% was below expectations and, among major Southeast Asian economies, stronger only than Thailand's.

Rwanda increased its policy rate 50 basis points to 8.75%, the highest since 2009 and its third successive hike. Urban inflation had remained in double digits since April and reached 14.5%, driven by fresh food, meat and energy. Forecasts of 13.1% inflation in 2026 and 7.9% in 2027 reflected continuing El Nino and Middle East risks; the target range is 2%–8%.

Australia's adjustment came in forecasts and bonds. Commonwealth Bank, ANZ and Goldman Sachs shifted toward a November increase after hot inflation data, while Deutsche Bank and NAB expected September. Markets fully priced 25 basis points by November and roughly even odds for September. Three-year government yields rose 7 basis points to 4.67%, a more-than-month high. July household spending rose 1.1% on the month and 7% annually. Some economists still expected no move, citing weak growth, falling house prices and the RBA's caution about monthly inflation figures.

BOJ Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino urged greater attention to upside price risks and did not resist expectations of a September increase. Swaps implied about an 82% probability, little changed by the speech. The yen briefly weakened to 159.40 per dollar as investors received no stronger commitment than they already expected. A September move would be the shortest interval between hikes under Kazuo Ueda. Himino said waiting for perfect information could force a sharper response later. Even so, a single hike may offer limited help to a currency burdened by rate differentials and oil imports: the yen had returned toward 160 after coordinated intervention moved it from roughly 164 to 155.23.

The ECB's July account showed that some members would have supported an increase and questioned whether another hike could be avoided, although all backed the hold. Officials debated a mildly restrictive setting to return inflation to 2%, with the deposit rate at 2.25% and Philip Lane placing the upper end of neutral at 2.5%. The account broadened the case for tightening without erasing concerns about doing too much.

Thailand's Vitai Ratanakorn pushed back against assumptions that the 1% rate would stay unchanged for a long time, while saying evidence was insufficient for a move now. Persistent inflation or sharp baht weakness could warrant a hike; a fresh economic shock could warrant a cut. Further easing might transmit poorly through banks and reduce depositor income and policy space. After the previous day's hold, the new emphasis was that policy remained genuinely two-way.

## UBS's AT1 alternative faces scrutiny as Vanke's losses deepen

Swiss lawmakers are considering redesigned AT1 bonds as a cheaper way for UBS to meet part of roughly $20 billion in additional capital requirements. The government wants foreign subsidiaries fully backed by common equity Tier 1. UBS represents about 7% of the €286 billion European AT1 market, making the design relevant well beyond one issuer.

An academic framework informing the parliamentary discussion would suspend AT1 coupons, dividends and management bonuses when the bank fell below regulatory capital requirements. If that failed to restore capital, holders could be offered voluntary equity conversion alongside a rights issue. The aim is to absorb losses while the bank is still operating, rather than only at rescue or resolution. Credit Suisse's $17 billion AT1 write-off remains a source of litigation and investor concern.

Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter regards common equity as the only reliable going-concern loss absorber, and the SNB supports full CET1 backing of foreign units. Any alternative also needs international regulatory and investor acceptance. The upper-house economic committee is due to consider the issue on August 31, with parliament ultimately deciding. This is a proposal, not an agreed change in existing AT1 terms.

China Vanke's first-half loss widened to 14.95 billion yuan from 11.95 billion a year earlier, bringing cumulative losses since 2024 to 153 billion. Working capital remained tight despite extensions of 10 public bonds. Shenzhen Metro lent more than 30 billion yuan last year and another 4.5 billion in the first half, helping fund upfront payments for extensions without restoring operating cash generation. Vanke's 3.975% dollar bond traded near 55 cents and its 3.5% note near 51.

An extended 3% yuan bond, originally due late last year, now matures in mid-December. Vanke said it would prepare repayment plans, including possible extensions, for public bonds due through next June. Shenzhen authorities installed a board dominated by state-linked executives, but the size and priority of further shareholder support remained unclear.

In US high-yield municipal issuance, buyers rejected weak deals even before distress. Issuers raised $3.3 billion this year, about 5% below the prior year's record pace, while overall municipal issuance ran roughly 6% ahead. Houston nonprofit QCF/I shelved an unrated deal after bankers lifted the proposed yield to 8%; another unrated project also failed to sell. Higher yields on stronger credits and tighter compensation for lower quality reduced buyers' incentive to stretch. Thirty-three first-time defaults totaling $2.81 billion were still close to historical experience, so the failed offerings did not indicate a market-wide closure.

## Colombia's debt-service bill rises; Indonesia and India face currency pressures

Colombia's new administration plans to restore the fiscal rule in 2028 after its predecessor suspended it, and to propose legislation reducing the primary deficit by 2.2 percentage points of GDP. The immediate budget is much more difficult: the 2027 overall deficit is projected at 9.4% of GDP, with spending up 16% to 635 trillion pesos, about $201 billion.

Debt service would jump more than 50% to 155 trillion pesos, alongside 393 trillion of operating spending and 87 trillion of investment. Planned borrowing totals about 239 trillion pesos, 63% domestic and 37% overseas. The government says it is recognizing liabilities understated by its predecessor. Greater transparency and a future fiscal rule may help credibility, but investors still have to finance the near-term increase in interest expense and borrowing before the adjustment takes effect.

Thousands protested at Indonesia's parliament over corruption, living costs and accountability. Lawmakers promised to enact an asset-forfeiture law by December 15 or resign, helping calm the crowd after afternoon tensions. The rupiah closed 0.1% weaker at 17,726 per dollar after falling as much as 0.4%. Ten-year yields rose 3 basis points to 7.08%, extending bond losses to a third day; equities finished 1.8% higher as fears of broader violence receded.

The protest coalition was smaller and less unified than the nationwide movement a year earlier, with major student and labor groups absent. That helped the intraday recovery. Some investors had already rotated from rupiah bonds into dollar debt, showing a preference to reduce currency exposure without necessarily exiting the sovereign.

India's central bank has intervened more routinely when the rupee weakens, supported by $73 billion of dollar inflows since June. It spent $7 billion on one day last month. The operations helped bring near-term rupee volatility close to a 10-month low, even as higher oil widened the current-account deficit and the US rate differential narrowed. Smoother trading does not remove the import bill or the reserve cost of defending the currency.

## Payroll revisions and Warsh arrive together; financing terms follow

The simultaneous August 28 payroll revision and Warsh address will make it important to distinguish a change in the historical employment baseline from the chair's interpretation of inflation. A large downward revision could support patience, while a speech endorsing Schmid and Hammack's view of insufficient restraint would pull in the opposite direction. The 2- to 5-year sector is most directly exposed to a change in the expected hike date.

Australia's Q2 GDP and labor releases will test whether stronger spending and inflation outweigh weak housing. In Japan, Ueda's expected remarks after the G20 gathering, followed by Hajime Takata and Kazuyuki Masu, will indicate how comfortable officials are with a shorter interval between hikes. Both markets already price substantial tightening, making the degree of confirmation important.

For credit, Volta's proposed $5 billion package still needs terms linking the Anthropic contract to collateral, amortization and sponsor support. Switzerland's August 31 committee discussion will show whether the AT1 alternative advances or the preference for common equity prevails. Neither a long customer contract nor a proposed capital instrument settles the allocation of losses until the actual terms are known.
